cards.heading: Cravings have a timer
cards.body: Research shows that almost all cravings peak within 20 minutes and then decrease — whether you use or not. The craving literally runs out of fuel.

cards.question: What is the most effective thing to do when a craving peaks?

options.text: White-knuckle it and fight the urge
Give in to prevent it getting worse

cards.explanation: Distraction is key. You don't need to fight the craving — just survive the peak. After 20 minutes, the wave has passed.

cards.heading: The distraction strategy
cards.body: Anything that fully engages your brain for 20 minutes works: a walk, a phone call, a game, a cold shower. The goal isn't to feel great — just to outlast the peak.

cards.statement: Fighting a craving directly is more effective than distracting yourself.
cards.explanation: Suppressing cravings directly often backfires — it keeps the craving in focus. Distraction shifts attention away, letting the craving fade naturally.

cards.prompt: What's one activity you could do right now that would fully occupy your brain for 20 minutes? Write it down so you're ready next time.
